text.content:
Easy. A sleepy village that has never had a real monster.

Lantern Night: Pies left on doorsteps “for the wanderers”.

The shopping list (4 items):

  1. A wheel of strong cheese (essential)
  2. Seed potatoes
  3. Knitting wool
  4. An almanac with next year’s moons

The furniture: a stuffed bear (Bulky: one carrier), at the tavern cellar (1).

Villagers: the baker’s wife (looking for a lost cat); the night watchman (tipsy from the cider).

Easy: Suspicion Limit 9 · Difficulty: the way out 6, the lock-up 10 · the final flight: mob 10, Lead 2, escape at 5.

In Foundry

Puddlecombe is ready to play. Set up a ready-made game (Configure Settings, or the question when a world first opens) brings it in, each part in a folder named Puddlecombe: this entry, the scene Puddlecombe (its night map, with a pin on each place that opens its page here), the macro Puddlecombe: Start the Raid, and the eight Entities with tokens if the world hasn’t got them.

Run the macro as the Storyteller once each player owns their Entity: a new Easy raid, with this list on the Raid HUD. The party’s tokens start on the map’s yard at The Way Out. The macro runs this:

// Puddlecombe: a new Easy raid, with Puddlecombe's shopping list on the Raid HUD.
// Run it as the Storyteller once each player owns their Entity: the raid takes every Entity with a player owner.
return game.dontGetForked.raid.start({
  town: "Puddlecombe", difficulty: "easy",
  list: [
    { name: "a wheel of strong cheese", duty: "cook", essential: true },
    { name: "seed potatoes", duty: "gardener", essential: false },
    { name: "knitting wool", duty: "tailor", essential: false },
    { name: "an almanac with next year’s moons", duty: "librarian", essential: false }
  ],
});

Each location’s rows run in order: its two ways in (picked by the first roll at one of them, then kept for the raid), then each “Then”. The furniture’s obstacle is already 2 harder. It comes last, marked “for the piece”. Watched: Trouble there gets you caught. (group): each Entity rolls for itself. The loud way works too, at Suspicion +1 whatever the result. The kind in brackets is what one Castle Duty shops for. Any move takes one Turn (one more carrying furniture).

The way out (Sly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way) and the lock-up (Sly, or Brawn the loud way; Nimble too to slip free) are always watched.

Easy: Difficulty: the lock-up 10.

While held, you can’t pick up or be handed anything. You can still spend charges on any roll at the lock-up (your own, a rescuer’s or another captive’s).

At the lock-upRescueSlipping free
Who rollsAnyone who isn’t held, at the lock-up (getting there is a move)The captive, as its action, once per Turn, from the Turn after its capture
TraitsSly, or Brawn the loud waySly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way
DifficultyThe lock-up’s: 10The lock-up’s: 10
SuccessEvery captive there is freeYou’re free
CostEvery captive there is free (the Storyteller picks a Cost as usual)Nothing happens
TroubleSuspicion +1, and the rescuer is caught: a local chaseSuspicion +1, but no chase
ThenThe freed act again next Turn, from the lock-upYou act again next Turn, from the lock-up

The lock-up is always watched, so abilities that need a watched obstacle (Dracula’s Mesmerise) work on both. A rescue frees only the captives held at that moment, so anyone captured later needs a new rescue.

The first time anyone reaches a watched location, the Storyteller makes a Tell check: roll a d6, and on 4–6 a Tell goes off. Each place is checked once a raid, for everyone. The lock-up counts, but not a captive’s arrival.

In Foundry: a capture shows on the Raid HUD at the lock-up. From the next Turn a captive’s roll is slipping free (tick At the lock-up: slipping free); a rescue that beats the lock-up frees every captive there.

The way out (Sly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way) and the lock-up (Sly, or Brawn the loud way; Nimble too to slip free) are always watched.

Easy: Difficulty: the way out 6.

The way out is one watched obstacle: Sly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way, at Difficulty 6 on Easy, 8 on Standard and 10 on Hard. The party leaves together. One Entity rolls for everyone, but only when every Entity who isn’t captured is at the way out. A Success or a Cost gets everyone out, and a Cost here costs nothing. On Trouble, Suspicion rises and the roller is caught. The way out can be rolled once a Turn, so try again next Turn. Anyone still captured is left behind.

The party starts at the edge of town, at the way out, and entering the town needs no roll.

The first time anyone reaches a watched location, the Storyteller makes a Tell check: roll a d6, and on 4–6 a Tell goes off. Each place is checked once a raid, for everyone. The way out counts once anyone comes back to it.

In Foundry: the party’s tokens start on this yard. The roll dialog has a tick for the way out.
